newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close at record high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close at record high.

text.p: Swiss shares shrugged off the weaker bias on most European bourses to finish at a second consecutive all-time closing high, boosted by U.S. dollar strength and derivatives-linked buying, share dealers said.
"Trade is likely to remain hectic through Friday," one trader noted.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index closed up 50.4 points, or 1.13 percent, at 4,514.6 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index added 26.76 points, or 0.94 percent, to end at 2,866.19.
Dollar-sensitive stocks such as SMH, Nestle, Novartis and Roche were among the winners on the day.
SMH bearer shares jumped 35 francs, or 3.7 percent, to 982. One dealer said SMH's watch joint venture with Calvin Klein may have also triggered buys.
Novartis registered shares ended up 17 francs at 1,764.

UBS bearer shares soared 26 francs to 1,319. Dealers said UBS's solid performance recently could be partially explained by the fact that it broke technical resistance at 1,260. The bank will release its 1996 figures on Friday. CS Group and SBC were also higher.

Major insurers Swiss Re, Winterthur and Zurich posted advances of around one percent each. Swiss Re was up 15 francs to 1,480. Winterthur firmed 10 francs to 883 and Zurich ended up 5.50 francs at 432.
Electrowatt, Holderbank, Adecco and Swissair all closed lower.
